ERW Pipe Size Chart
ERW Pipe Size Chart
This page provides a complete 
ERW Pipe Size Chart
 covering outside diameter (OD), wall thickness (WT), inside diameter (ID), and weight per meter for all standard pipe sizes and schedules. The data is presented as per international standards ASME B36.10M and Indian standard IS 1239, available in both metric (mm) and imperial (inch) formats for easy reference.
Sachiya Steel International
is a trusted manufacturer and supplier of ERW black and galvanized steel pipes. Our products are produced at our ISO 9001:2015 & TÜV-certified facility in Vasai, Thane (Mumbai) and supplied to customers across more than 85 countries worldwide with consistent quality and timely delivery.
What is ERW Pipe?
ERW stands for Electric Resistance Welded pipe. It is manufactured by passing a flat steel strip (hot-rolled coil) through forming rollers that shape it into a round pipe. The edges are then joined together using high-frequency electric resistance welding, without any filler material. This process creates a strong longitudinal weld seam along the length of the pipe.
ERW pipes are made in standard dimensions as per ASME B36.10M, which means they match seamless pipes in size, schedule, and fitting compatibility. However, the manufacturing process is different. ERW pipes are more cost-effective and are commonly used in construction, structural work, plumbing, and moderate-pressure industrial applications, while seamless pipes are preferred for high-pressure and high-temperature critical services.
Common standards for ERW pipes include ASTM A53, API 5L, IS 1239, IS 3589, EN 10217-1, and ASTM A500, which define material properties, testing requirements, and usage conditions.

ERW Pipe Weight Formula
The weight per metre of an ERW steel pipe is calculated using the same formula as seamless pipe:
W (kg/m) = 0.02466 × T × (D − T)
Where: W = Weight per metre (kg/m) D = Outside diameter (mm) T = Wall thickness (mm) 0.02466 = Density constant for carbon steel (7.85 g/cm³)
Example:
 For a 3″ NPS Sch 40 ERW pipe — OD = 88.90 mm, WT = 5.49 mm: W = 0.02466 × 5.49 × (88.90 − 5.49) W = 0.02466 × 5.49 × 83.41 
W = 11.29 kg/m
For ERW pipes with a weld joint efficiency factor applied (ASME B31.3 / API 5L design), use E = 0.85 for standard ERW or E = 1.00 for DSAW/seamless when calculating allowable pressure.

ERW Pipe Wall Thickness Chart — Schedule Selection Guide
Choosing the right schedule is the most common decision in ERW pipe procurement. The schedule number determines how much pressure the pipe can safely handle at a given temperature. Higher schedule = thicker wall = smaller bore = higher pressure rating.

ERW pipe is generally available in Sch 5 through Sch 80 in standard production. Sch 120, 160, and XXS are typically produced as seamless for large-diameter sizes. For small-bore ERW pipe (NPS 1/2" to NPS 4"), Sch 80 ERW is widely available. For NPS 6" and above, verify schedule availability with the manufacturer.

FAQ – 
ERW Pipe Size Chart
Find quick answers about ERW pipe dimensions, schedules, standards, and weight references.
How to read the ERW pipe size chart? 
+
The chart shows nominal pipe size, actual outside diameter, wall thickness, inside diameter, and approximate weight per meter. Use the OD and WT columns together to identify the exact pipe required for your application.
What is the difference between NPS and OD? 
+
NPS is the nominal size designation, while OD is the actual outside diameter. For pipe sizes below NPS 14, the NPS number does not match the actual OD exactly.
Which schedule is most commonly used? 
+
Sch 40 is the most widely used schedule for general piping because it provides a good balance between strength, bore size, and availability. Sch 80 is selected when higher pressure capacity is needed.
What does kg/m mean in the chart? 
+
Kg/m means the approximate weight of one meter length of pipe. It helps in pricing, transport planning, and structural load calculations.
Which standard should I use for ERW pipe? 
+
The correct standard depends on the project. ASTM A53 and API 5L are common for international use, IS 1239 is common in India, and IS 3589 is used for large-diameter applications.
Can ERW pipe be used for pressure service? 
+
Yes, ERW pipe is used for pressure service when it meets the applicable standard and schedule requirement. The pressure capability depends on wall thickness, diameter, material grade, and service temperature.
Do you provide custom ERW pipe sizes? 
+
Custom sizes are commonly available depending on the required diameter, wall thickness, grade, and standard. These are usually supplied against drawing or project specification.
